differences.what: the street front's openings: the attic's paired lights, the pavilion's second-storey window, the door, the narrow light over its south jamb and the principal-storey window past the tree
differences.how: T-3156: the camera fitted to them (11.7 px rms); the render's openings fall within about 0.5 m of the print's, the attic's the furthest (the pavilion's place, below)

differences.what: the pavilion carried up an attic storey with its paired transomed lights under its own steep hipped roof, the roof running back into the mansard
differences.how: T-3156: the shallow pavilion's attic storey and K01's hipped crown raised onto it

differences.what: the pavilion and its attic stand about 0.5-0.7 m north of the print's, because K01 cannot cut the door through a projection (as on the square-on)

the corner bay runs about 0.75 m south of the main front's south corner: the print's cornice turns onto the flank at x 1605 px and the bay's south face shows at x 1745-1790 px; the build sets the bay flush with the flank (its corner at x 1618 px, the main corner at 1711)
the south flank is rock-faced random ashlar, dark against the smooth front; the build lays it in buff common brick
differences.how: T-3562: the flank laid in the front's K02 stone on the front's own beds, rock-faced to the profile's 25 mm (stone_front.flanks), its windows under flat arches and seated on stone sills; it renders as a broken stone face against the smooth front where it rendered buff brick. The print's broken-coursed random ashlar is laid as even courses on the front's lines: the joint pattern, under a visitor's notice

differences.what: the south flank's tall stack, carried up from the flank wall past the mansard with a panelled shaft and a corbelled head of flues (x 1740-1820 px)
differences.how: T-3561: rebuilt as the print's: K15's stone stack standing on the south cornice about 1.6 m back from the front, rising past the mansard to a corbelled head and cap at 14.45 m, with three tall pots in a row back from the street to about 15.2 m; measured from the cornice's corner it renders 83 px along the flank against the print's 73 px, and its pots' tops at y 75 px against 72 px

differences.what: the mansard's curb and cresting: the print's curb, under its cresting, stands about 0.8 m higher on this view than the build's; and the gabled dormer on the south flank's mansard (x 1820-1880 px), built by T-3562 just behind the stack (13.9 m from the rear, where it stood out of frame at 9.0 m), its sash and gable about 1 m lower than the print's with the curb
the main cornice's stone consoles, round the corner onto the flank
differences.how: T-3561: K10's scrolled consoles (wall_head.blocks) under the corona, 0.45 m high, 0.17 m wide, no more than 0.5 m apart, on a 0.32 m frieze; they render at y 405-440 px against the print's 400-432 px, and carry round the south-west corner and along the south flank as the oblique draws them

differences.what: the door's pedimented hood and the stoop's stone cheeks
differences.how: T-3562: the stone pediment on its brackets over the door, and the swept cheeks with a newel at each foot, as on the square-on (whose print shows both whole); here the tree's trunk crosses the hood

differences.what: the stoop's arched underside, the iron hand rail on its cheek and the basement doorway under the landing (x 1045-1260 px, y 960-1150 px)
the stone balcony's pierced panels on the bay's deck
differences.how: the panels' pattern is K08's, the rail's place and height the print's within a few pixels

differences.what: the street fence, the walk and the parkway's posts
the coping, posts and walk T-3206 lays
differences.how: seen obliquely the low coping and posts read as the print's low line; read square-on in chicagology_square_on

differences.what: the stack's sunk panels on its south face (x 1765-1825 px, about 11.35-13.45 m)
differences.how: not built: K15 lays a panel's recess in brick (k15_chimneys ROLE_MATERIAL 'panel'), which on a stone stack reads as brick strips; the kit module is an input to every K01 mesh, so the fix is a town rebake of its own

differences.what: the stack's pots: the print's stand about 1.1 m over the cap, three or four in a row
differences.how: three of the kit's tallest pot (0.72 m) stand on it; the 1.1 m stack takes three of K15's 0.21 m flues. T-3562 re-read it: the dark pots stand about 63-73 px over the cap (x 1730-1800, y 72-145 px), about 1.0-1.1 m, slender and fluted, with a lit fourth shape nearest the street that may be a fourth pot or the lit side of the head. A longer pot is a new profile in K15's kit (k15_chimneys.json), which every K01 house hashes as a mesh input (generators/mesh_inputs.py), so it is a whole-district rebake rather than this house's: it stays open here

differences.what: the rosettes over the cornice's consoles
differences.how: carved bosses about 0.12 m across in the cornice's bed, under the 0.3 m bar; not built

differences.what: the south flank's tone: the print draws the rock-faced flank darker than the front; a monochrome print cannot say whether that is another stone, soot or the light
differences.how: T-3562 lays it in the front's Lemont stone (L-k01-1815-sears-1893)

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
